answer: Staggered Arrival Window.** Identities enter a rotating queue: each request must arrive inside a slot derived from a slowly evolving seed shared among peers, and a late arrival waits for the next round like a dying ember. New identities face a longer settling delay before their traffic counts, acting as a basalt layer that pads early latency. Each valid slot advance gives a slow anchor against floods. An attacker must hold many identities through repeated idle rounds, paying real wall-clock delay and bandwidth per clone.
